subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Reading in detail: comprehension and reasons for over-shopping
outcomes: Read an article in detail and answer questions
Evaluate the reasons for over-shopping and its long-term effects

tf.s: The women can afford to spend a lot because they have very good jobs.
tf.why: They are a corporate lawyer and an accountant.

tf.s: Katy feels bad about spending because she thinks she does not deserve a treat.
tf.why: She thinks she deserves a treat for working hard.

tf.s: Clever marketing is one reason people buy things they do not need.
tf.why: Companies use clever marketing to make us buy.

tf.s: Shopping is a long-term solution to feeling bad.
tf.why: It is only a short-term fix.

tf.s: Over-shopping can create credit card debt.
tf.why: Spending too much can lead to debt.

tf.s: Lack of financial self-restraint can result in bankruptcy.
tf.why: The article says it can even lead to divorce.

tf.s: People who feel lonely or depressed may shop for consolation.
tf.why: Consolation means comfort when you feel sad.
Affluent means rich, having a lot of money.

tf.s: According to the article, shopping always makes people happy for months.
tf.why: It can make people feel bad for months because of debt.

tf.s: A 'short-term fix' helps only for a short time.
tf.why: It does not solve the problem for long.

boxes.q: Why can the women spend so much?

o: she thinks she deserves a treat
boxes.why: She rewards herself for working hard.

boxes.q: What feeling can make people shop for comfort?
boxes.why: Lonely or depressed people may shop for consolation.
A bargain costs less than usual.
Bankruptcy is a serious money problem.

boxes.q: Is shopping a short-term or long-term fix?
boxes.why: It helps only for a little while.
Companies market products to persuade us.
Affluent people have plenty of money.

boxes.q: What might lonely people shop for?
boxes.why: Shopping can feel comforting at first.

mcq.q: How can the women afford to spend so much money?
mcq.why: A corporate lawyer and an accountant earn well.

mcq.q: Which are two reasons people buy things they do not need?
mcq.why: The article gives these two reasons.

mcq.q: What can lack of financial self-restraint result in?
mcq.why: Not controlling spending leads to serious problems.

o: comfort for someone who is sad
mcq.why: Lonely or depressed people may shop for comfort.

mcq.q: Ali feels sad, so he buys new shoes. He feels happy for a day, then worries about money. This shows shopping is ______.
mcq.why: The good feeling does not last.

mcq.q: Katy says, 'I work hard, so I deserve a treat.' What is she doing?
o: giving a reason for her spending
mcq.why: She explains why she does not feel bad.

mcq.q: Which person is most likely to get credit card debt?
o: someone who buys things they cannot pay for
someone who pays in cash only
mcq.why: Debt comes from spending money you do not have.

mcq.q: Does shopping really improve our mood?
o: Only briefly; debts can make us feel bad for months
mcq.why: The article shows a short-term good feeling but long-term problems.

mcq.q: Why is shopping called a 'short-term fix' for feeling bad?
o: It creates more problems than it solves in the long run
It takes a short time to shop

mcq.q: Why might clever marketing make people buy things they do not need?
o: It persuades people that they want the product
